frontmatter.name: api-contract-change
frontmatter.description: Protect API routes, versions, bindings, status codes, authentication behavior, response shapes, and OpenAPI when controllers or public HTTP contracts change. Do not activate for internal refactors with no HTTP effect.

frontmatter.name: architecture-boundary-check
frontmatter.description: Detect forbidden project, namespace, and package dependencies after project-reference changes or code moves across Clean Architecture layers. Do not activate for isolated edits that cannot affect dependency direction.

frontmatter.name: dotnet-change-verification
frontmatter.description: Select and run proportionate restore, build, and test checks after changes to C#, project files, solution files, or .NET build configuration. Do not activate for documentation-only edits.

frontmatter.name: ef-migration
frontmatter.description: Create and validate an additive Entity Framework Core migration when an entity mapping or relational schema change requires one. Do not activate when no schema delta exists.

frontmatter.name: integration-adapter
frontmatter.description: Implement or modify a Redis, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, identity, localization, or other external-system adapter behind an application-owned port. Do not activate for pure application logic or vendor-free domain work.

frontmatter.name: package-upgrade
frontmatter.description: Research and stage a coherent NuGet, .NET SDK, or container package-family upgrade using current official sources. Do not activate for ordinary code changes without a version change.

frontmatter.name: architecture-reviewer
frontmatter.description: Review cross-layer changes for dependency direction and responsibility placement.

frontmatter.name: dependency-auditor
frontmatter.description: Independently verify package or container versions, advisories, compatibility, deprecations, and support status.

frontmatter.name: integration-test-reviewer
frontmatter.description: Review integration and functional tests for isolation, determinism, and external-service assumptions.
